question: Why does the post-seek resume with 16 MiB pieces take about twice the line-rate time for the gsp02-v2 candidates?
method: thin/16MiB/30Mbit, C0 (legacy) and C2 (edges+upstream), 3 runs each, SPDIAG timelines aligned to the seek request (shared CLOCK_MONOTONIC); plus the gsp02-v2 per-run seek distribution.
findings: Refuted: the previous stream does not hold an urgent piece at a seek. It notices the disconnect at once (~0 ms), ends and is destroyed; right after the seek only the new position's piece (32) is urgent.

The post-seek time is bimodal for every variant: ~3.4 s (one 16 MiB piece at the 5 MB/s line rate) or ~6.5-9.6 s. In the slow runs another window piece (33 or 35) finished first at full speed: the two peers worked on different pieces, so the piece the player waits for got half the bandwidth.

The candidates fall into the slow mode more often (gsp02-v2 thin/16MiB fast-mode runs: C0 6/10, C1 1/10, C2 2/10): a systematic effect of the policy on libtorrent's piece/peer assignment, not chance alone.

Tracebacks: 0 in these 14 runs (8 in the traceback cell fast/4MiB/8Mbit); 32 diagnostic runs without one so far versus ~1.7 % of gate runs. Next gate runs keep the masked traceback capture on (no effect on the measurement).
next: gsp02-v3 candidate 'focus': while the piece a stream is waiting for is missing, only that piece gets a deadline (all peers on it), then the legacy tight window; dropped deadline pieces return to the background priority (G0 leak fix); start with upstream edges (1+1).
